claim: The laboratory's ambient temperature is 20 degrees Celsius, read off a thermometer by the operator. Because nothing actuates the sample temperature on this instrument, this is an ambient value of the room rather than a setpoint -- which is what makes it an operator reading at E3 and not a calibration at E2.

numbers.name: ambient_temperature
numbers.note: the reading was reported as 20 degrees Celsius. The store carries kelvin because the unit registry is multiplicative -- si_factor and a dimension vector cannot express an offset unit, so Celsius cannot enter it at all. 293 K rather than 293.15 K: the exact conversion would claim five figures from a reading given to the nearest degree, and the 0.15 K it drops is far inside the resolution of the reading.

validity_conditions: The room as of 2026-09-17, operator read off a thermometer. Two things are still open and neither may be assumed. WHERE the thermometer is -- room air or close to the sample -- is not recorded, so this is the laboratory's ambient temperature and it is not established to be the sample's; a plan that needs the viscosity or the thermal energy AT THE SAMPLE stands on that gap rather than on this entry. And the drift band is unmeasured: with no actuator, that band is not a tolerance anyone chooses but a property of the room somebody has to measure. Water's viscosity moves by roughly two percent per kelvin, so in explore mode a drift of about a kelvin does not move a decade and can be ignored, while in confirm mode it cannot. The date the reading was taken is not recorded either -- what is dated 2026-09-17 is the operator's statement that it is a reading.
